notes.hreflangDecision: Use hreflang='es' and <html lang='es'>. Not es-419, and not regional codes. Reasons: (1) Google's documentation says codes outside ISO 639-1 / ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 'such as es-419, aren't supported'. (2) There is one Spanish version for all five markets, and a language-only 'es' tag matches Spanish users in every region, Spain included. es-MX alone would leave Spain, Argentina and Colombia on x-default. (3) Autocomplete is almost the same across markets: 384 of 464 market/seed pairs in batch 1 returned exactly the Mexico list, and most differences were one extra long-tail item. (4) Every Spanish competitor checked (KlickPin, SavePin, PinDown, PinterestVideo, Publer, VidAU) declares plain 'es'. Wire it as pairs: each English page lists hreflang='en' (itself) + hreflang='es' (/es/<slug>) + x-default (English); each Spanish page lists the same three. Skipped pages get no 'es' alternate. og:locale es_LA with og:locale:alternate es_ES.
notes.urlStructure: /es for the home page and /es/<spanish-slug> for the rest. Lowercase ASCII, hyphens, accents and ñ stripped ('imagenes', 'como'), no trailing slash (matches normalizeCanonical). Spanish slugs repeat the query words in the URL and breadcrumb. SavePin and the editorial guides use Spanish slugs; KlickPin and PinDown keep English slugs under /es/. Add the /es routes to SITEMAP_ROUTES with xhtml:link alternates.
notes.neutralSpanish: Write one neutral Latin American Spanish that Spain also reads naturally. Use tú. Spell it 'video', not 'vídeo': every Spanish query collected, from Spain included, types 'video', and the RAE accepts both. Device words: 'celular' in titles, 'móvil' once in body copy. 'PC'/'computadora' in titles, 'ordenador'/'portátil' once in the PC guide. Use 'enlace' as Pinterest's UI does, with 'link' once per page. No voseo (AR) and no vosotros (ES).
notes.marketDifferences: Autocomplete differences between markets are small long-tail additions: ES adds 'para macbook', 'en linea', 'videos online', 'pc'; AR and CO add 'save pin', 'con enlace', 'por enlace', 'sin registrarse', 'para editar'; US Hispanic adds 'en galería', 'en el celular', 'sin aplicaciones', 'chrome', and English phrasings ('pinterest video downloader para iphone', 'without watermark'). typography.accentCollision: Line-height is the real problem. Cap height is 0.80em, but accented capitals (Á É Í Ó Ú) reach 0.979em and Ñ reaches 0.961em. The display H1 is set at line-height 0.88–0.9, so an accent on line 2 rises about 0.08–0.10em into the baseline of line 1 and touches the letters above. An opening '¿' or '¡' descends to −0.21em and hits the caps of the next line. On the first line, accents also stick out about 0.14em above the line box, so any overflow:hidden or tight padding-top crops them. Fix: ':lang(es) h1, :lang(es) .article-title, :lang(es) .display { line-height: 1 }' (0.98 at minimum), no overflow:hidden on headline wrappers, and no ¿ at the start of display H1s. The proposed H1s are statements and avoid it, but FAQ H3s in system sans are fine with ¿.
typography.uppercase: text-transform: uppercase keeps the accents. Spanish requires accents on capitals (RAE), so write the source text with the accents and never strip them for the gothic. With <html lang='es'> the browser uppercases correctly.
